stations_frame: s = metres from the junction node at the start of each leg, along the OSM forward leg (EXPANSION-PLAN 'Stations'); left / right offsets + = left of the forward direction

paint.centre: measured off NAIP (repair round 2): a raised concrete island st 32-118 then the hatched teardrop to ~172 on the J4 approach; the painted double-double-yellow median 1.7-6.6 m wide, ~1.6 m LEFT of the road's middle on the 1 km climb (the lanes are uneven: one down, two up), opening into left-turn pockets at the side streets; a plain double yellow where it narrows (Hemingway st ~380-520, st ~1500-1545, Park Ridge st ~1620-1710)
paint.lanes: 2 + 2 (1 down / 2 up on the 763 m way)

correction.what: Princess View's raised median MD7, right face over the tree-shadow run lap v533-v542 (piece B s 622.5-647.5)
correction.why: the automatic aerial reader read two street trees standing in the median (crowns + westward shadows, NAIP 2022 z18) as island: the right face swung 3.6 <-> 5.9 m wide; the left face held at +1.4..+1.9 m
correction.measured: the PC, 2026-11-04: NAIP 2022 z18 (source/naip_2022_lm_z18.jpg) on scripts-v021 projection.py's WGS84 series, calibrated to the built faces on the clear run v543-v556 (offset -2.58 m), line fit of the right face -3.45 m at v535 -> -3.38 m at v556 (lap frame), sd 0.35 m; files D:/k10-scratch/lm_phase2/naip/edges.txt, pv_table.txt, step3b_read.txt
correction.method: the right face of every piece-B row whose lap vertex lies in [533, 542] set to the line fit (extrapolated to v533-v534); the left face kept; width and offset recomputed; the islands and the median edge paint re-derived with tools/expansion_pieces.decorate's formula

correction.what: Mission Gorge Rd's raised median on piece C, set to its two curb faces as the 2024 lidar has them at every 2.5 m station it covers: the island's real width and place, the Margerum Avenue / Mission Vista Drive crossing (no median between two noses, a narrow strip beside each turn pocket), and the J3 end (MD11 on its real line and to its real end, the two openings where they are, MD12 where it stands, MD13 from its real start)
correction.why: the plan's median is linear between eye readings 250 m apart, centred on the middle of road edges read by eye to +-1.0-1.5 m: MD13 was declared, and built, unbroken across a real crossing whose two side streets are built stubs; its two openings near J3 stand about 13 m from the real ones (tools/author_expansion.py GAPS 174 / 202; the dossier's station labels run about 14.6 m ahead of s on this piece: my reading of two numbers, not traced in the dossier); and where it is whole it is wider than the real island and off its place
correction.measured: the G10, 2026-11-23: USGS CA_SanDiegoCo_D24 lidar (flown 2024-11), mg_median_faces_g10.py -> mg_median_faces.lidar.g10.json (its .md is the method and its checks). Per station the island's left and right curb face in the piece frame, each placed between the two neighbouring returns where the fewest fall on the wrong side (+- half that gap, a median 0.03 m), or 'none', or 'unclear'. Not measured there: the lidar's absolute horizontal accuracy (the NAD83(2011) -> WGS84 step is the null transform, stated to 2 m)
correction.method: piece C rows at the stations the lidar covers set to its faces (the median of three neighbouring stations per face; an unclear station from the nearest clear lidar); the island's place by the G10's 50 m bins of the road's outer curbs (edges true: the lidar's place; edges off: its middle from the real road's middle, set from the plan's road's middle; too few readings: the shift between the nearest called bins); the J3 end at the lidar's place; the medians' rings re-cut at those stations with the generator's nose rule and kept at the others; the island and the paint re-derived by tools/expansion_pieces.decorate (piece C's output only); the two centre lines cleared where there is no median
correction.the_photo_method_and_its_error: the PC first measured this off NAIP 2022 (faces_md.py, faces_piece.py; README.md): per station the excess R - G summed across the island, and its centroid. Its raw readings agree with the lidar (strip B's middle -2.24 against -2.32; within 0.22 m on the reference stretches). I then added +0.30 m of width and +0.49 m of middle, taken from s 930-985 and 1215-1260 on the assumption that the island fills its declared band there. It does not: the lidar has it 0.61 m narrower and 0.86 m right of that band. The strips built from the corrected photo were 1.96 and 1.84 m wide with their middles 0.70 and 0.58 m left of where the lidar has them; the lidar's are 1.24 and 1.30 m
correction.inferred: the offset of a row with no median (it only spaces the lane lines across an opening) runs straight between the islands either side. The shift of a 50 m bin with too few curb readings is interpolated between the nearest called bins. BLEND_M, the return to the declared faces where the lidar's coverage ends inside an island, is invented (with both lidar files no such place is left)
correction.not_built: MD12: the lidar has it at s 195-207.5, up to 3.6 m wide; four connector points lie inside it and the median tool and the lap's corridor build an island on six or more. Its place is set (the plan's painted outline lies where the real island stands); the island itself is owed. MD11 before s 45: the lidar has the island from s 25; the built one, and the north lap's nose at J3, start at s 45; owed

centre_paint_where_there_is_no_median.what: no centre line: the two lines decorate's rule draws where a road has no median are cleared at the points between the crossing's noses and in the two openings near J3
centre_paint_where_there_is_no_median.measured: the PC, 2026-11-23, NAIP 2022 z18 full mosaic. The crossing: within 3 m of the declared centre over s 1090-1112.5 (ten stations) the yellowest pixel reads (R + G) / 2 - B = +3.5 to +7.5, the asphalt 5-8 m either side +1.5 to +5.5. The openings: within 4 m of where the islands either side stand, s 187.5-192.5 and s 212.5-217.5 read +4.0 to +5.5 against the asphalt's +2.0 to +4.5; the stations beside the noses read +8 to +14 on light grey pixels (red, green and blue within 16 of each other: not yellow). What a double yellow reads at this resolution was not measured on this photo, so the reading is 'no yellower than the asphalt', not a threshold passed

The crossing: within 3 m of the declared centre over s 1090-1112.5 (ten stations) the yellowest pixel reads (R + G) / 2 - B = +3.5 to +7.5, the asphalt 5-8 m either side +1.5 to +5.5. The openings: within 4 m of where the islands either side stand, s 187.5-192.5 and s 212.5-217.5 read +4.0 to +5.5 against the asphalt's +2.0 to +4.5; the stations beside the noses read +8 to +14 on light grey pixels (red, green and blue within 16 of each other: not yellow). What a double yellow reads at this resolution was not measured on this photo, so the reading is 'no yellower than the asphalt', not a threshold passed

correction.what: Mission Gorge Rd's raised median on piece C, set to its two curb faces as the 2024 lidar has them at every 2.5 m station it covers: the island's real width and place, the Margerum Avenue / Mission Vista Drive crossing (no median between two noses, a narrow strip beside each turn pocket), and the J3 end (MD11 on its real line and to its real end, the two openings where they are, MD12 where it stands, MD13 from its real start)
correction.why: the plan's median is linear between eye readings 250 m apart, centred on the middle of road edges read by eye to +-1.0-1.5 m: MD13 was declared, and built, unbroken across a real crossing whose two side streets are built stubs; its two openings near J3 stand about 13 m from the real ones (tools/author_expansion.py GAPS 174 / 202; the dossier's station labels run about 14.6 m ahead of s on this piece: my reading of two numbers, not traced in the dossier); and where it is whole it is wider than the real island and off its place
correction.measured: the G10, 2026-11-23: USGS CA_SanDiegoCo_D24 lidar (flown 2024-11), mg_median_faces_g10.py -> mg_median_faces.lidar.g10.json (its .md is the method and its checks). Per station the island's left and right curb face in the piece frame, each placed between the two neighbouring returns where the fewest fall on the wrong side (+- half that gap, a median 0.03 m), or 'none', or 'unclear'. Not measured there: the lidar's absolute horizontal accuracy (the NAD83(2011) -> WGS84 step is the null transform, stated to 2 m)
correction.method: piece C rows at the stations the lidar covers set to its faces (the median of three neighbouring stations per face; an unclear station from the nearest clear lidar); the island's place by the G10's 50 m bins of the road's outer curbs (edges true: the lidar's place; edges off: its middle from the real road's middle, set from the plan's road's middle; too few readings: the shift between the nearest called bins); the J3 end at the lidar's place; the medians' rings re-cut at those stations with the generator's nose rule and kept at the others; the island and the paint re-derived by tools/expansion_pieces.decorate (piece C's output only); the two centre lines cleared where there is no median
correction.the_photo_method_and_its_error: the PC first measured this off NAIP 2022 (faces_md.py, faces_piece.py; README.md): per station the excess R - G summed across the island, and its centroid. Its raw readings agree with the lidar (strip B's middle -2.24 against -2.32; within 0.22 m on the reference stretches). I then added +0.30 m of width and +0.49 m of middle, taken from s 930-985 and 1215-1260 on the assumption that the island fills its declared band there. It does not: the lidar has it 0.61 m narrower and 0.86 m right of that band. The strips built from the corrected photo were 1.96 and 1.84 m wide with their middles 0.70 and 0.58 m left of where the lidar has them; the lidar's are 1.24 and 1.30 m
correction.inferred: the offset of a row with no median (it only spaces the lane lines across an opening) runs straight between the islands either side. The shift of a 50 m bin with too few curb readings is interpolated between the nearest called bins. BLEND_M, the return to the declared faces where the lidar's coverage ends inside an island, is invented (with both lidar files no such place is left)
correction.not_built: MD12: the lidar has it at s 195-207.5, up to 3.6 m wide; four connector points lie inside it and the median tool and the lap's corridor build an island on six or more. Its place is set (the plan's painted outline lies where the real island stands); the island itself is owed. MD11 before s 45: the lidar has the island from s 25; the built one, and the north lap's nose at J3, start at s 45; owed
